_source: Hand-verified directly against RCA-DFC-REG-002.md's real per-field bit tables (0x3000-0x301C), cited by contract ID below -- same disclosed scope/rationale as every prior field-map file's own _source note (extract_registers.py does not currently preserve per-field bit ranges project-wide). RTL012_EVT_OVERFLOW_STATUS's status_registers entry below (EVENT_OVERFLOW/DROP_COUNT mapped to the generic status_o.event_overflow/event_drop_count fields dfc_rtl012_status_t carries) closes the readback gap from the start, same discipline rtl006/007/008/009/010/011_field_map.json established (OPEN_ISSUES.md item 21). WDOG_STATUS's four W1C fields (SERVICE_ACCEPTED/EARLY_SERVICE/BAD_SERVICE_KEY/TIMEOUT) each appear in BOTH control_registers (their real clear-request fields) AND status_registers (their real sticky-readback fields), same dual-appearance pattern already used for every prior module's own multi-field W1C status registers. dfc_rtl012_control_t grew 110->111 bits this session (approved before implementation) to add rtl012_evt_overflow_status__event_overflow at the new highest bit (110), closing the eleventh real instance of the EVENT_OVERFLOW-clear-field gap class (items 2/7/8/12/20/24/28/32/36/43). Confirmed directly against dfc_registers_pkg.json: WDOG_STATUS/WDOG_ELAPSED_US/RTL012_EVT_OVERFLOW_STATUS are all readback=external; WDOG_CONTROL/WDOG_WINDOW_OPEN_US/WDOG_TIMEOUT_US are readback=internal_reg (plain RW, host read returns RTL-001's own stored value, not an RTL-012 echo -- no status_registers entry needed, same pattern as every other module's plain configuration RW registers); WDOG_SERVICE/WDOG_RECOVERY are readback=zero (WO-CMD, reads zero per REG-300C/REG-3018's own 'Reads zero' text -- forwarded via control_registers' command_pulse capture only, no status_registers entry).
